headline_findings: US tariff timeline after the IEEPA ruling: a Section 122 balance-of-payments surcharge of 10% ran from 24 Feb 2026 to 24 Jul 2026 (150-day statutory life; the announced rise to 15% was never enacted; the Court of International Trade struck Section 122 tariffs down in May 2026 but practical impact was limited). [secondary: Skadden May 2026; tariff-tool blogs]

Replacement in force since 24 Jul 2026: new Section 301 duties of 10% / 12.5% on products of roughly 60 economies (about 99.4% of US imports; 10% for economies with at least partial forced-labor import protections, 12.5% for the rest). [secondary: tariffstool.com / tarifftax.org blogs; verify against the Federal Register]

India is treated as a bilateral-deal country: blog sources say the bilateral deal rate (15%, i.e. 5 points above the 10% standard surcharge) replaces the surcharge for India-origin goods; the India policy lens separately found an interim US-India deal (2 Feb 2026) that cut the reciprocal rate to 18%. The two figures conflict; the India-origin US duty for HTS 8517.62 as of Sept 2026 is therefore ⚠ 15-18% (blog-grade) and must be verified against the Federal Register / CBP CSMS before any landed-cost decision. Whether the April 2025 electronics exemption for 8517.62 carries over to the Section 122/301 regime was not found. [estimate]

FDA issued a revised General Wellness Policy for Low Risk Devices on 6 Jan 2026 (supersedes Sept 2019). Wearables that estimate physiological parameters qualify if non-invasive, not intended for diagnosis/treatment, not a substitute for a cleared device, no outputs that guide clinical management, and no clinically-mimicking values unless validated. A screenless HR/HRV/sleep/readiness band fits; SpO2 or blood-pressure "insights" framed clinically do not. [verified via multiple law-firm alerts: Covington, Faegre Drinker, Troutman, ArentFox Schiff]

India export incentive: RoDTEP rates generally 0.3%-4.3% of FOB; DGFT Notification 60/2025-26 cut rates/caps to 50% for chapters 25+ (then restored to pre-23 Feb 2026 levels for exports between 23 Feb and 31 Mar 2026); the specific rate for HS 8517.62 was not found (consult DGFT Appendix 4R). [secondary: Afleo, efiletax]

Ultrahuman's first India factory: a search snippet places the first UltraFactory in Bengaluru in 2022; no source found for an Indore plant. Treat 'Indore' as unconfirmed. [secondary; not found for Indore]

Predictable Designs (John Teel): certification cost for an electronic product ranges from a few thousand dollars to about $50,000, driven mainly by how wireless is implemented (module vs custom radio); recommends funding certification and the first run via pre-orders/Kickstarter. [secondary: predictabledesigns.com]

Probe search (subagent, 14 Sep 2026): tariff-tracker blogs state that during the Section 122 window (24 Feb-24 Jul 2026) India-origin goods paid the same 10% as everyone else, not the 18% negotiated in the 2 Feb 2026 interim deal; after 24 Jul 2026 the Section 301 country-tier regime (10%/12.5%) applies with bilateral-deal countries possibly on a 15% deal rate. Net: the India-origin surcharge for Sept 2026 is ⚠ somewhere in 10-18% depending on source; the White House US-India Joint Statement (Feb 2026) and CBP CSMS messages are the primary documents to check. [secondary/blog: tariffstool.com India tariff page; Global Trade Alert S122 report; verified existence: whitehouse.gov joint statement]

detailed_notes:
# Policy supplement (main-session searches, 2026-09-14)

## US tariff regime, Sept 2026 (best available)
1. IEEPA tariffs ended after the Supreme Court ruling (see india-policy-trade lens: collection stopped 24 Feb 2026).
2. Section 122 surcharge: 10% from 24 Feb 2026, expired 24 Jul 2026 (150 days). Announced 15% never enacted. CIT struck the surcharge down in May 2026 (Skadden) with limited practical effect.
3. From 24 Jul 2026: Section 301 duties of 10% / 12.5% on ~60 economies (tariff-tool blogs). Bilateral-deal countries, India included, get their deal rate instead; one blog states 15% for India; the India policy lens found an 18% interim-deal reciprocal rate (Feb 2026). CONFLICT: use ⚠ 15-18% and verify.
4. China-origin fitness bands (HTS 8517.62.00): Section 301 List 4A 7.5% survives, plus whatever the 2026 Section 301 country tier adds; Whoop's own imports are classified under 9031.90.9195 with 9903.88.01 (competitors lens). Origin is decided by substantial transformation: populate the PCBA in India to obtain India origin.
5. HTS 8517.62.00 was exempt from the IEEPA reciprocal tariff (April 2025 electronics exemption). Whether any exemption exists under the Section 122/301 regime: not found.

## FDA
Revised General Wellness Policy for Low Risk Devices, 6 Jan 2026. A band that reports HR, HRV, sleep, skin temperature trend, strain and readiness with wellness framing is outside device regulation (no 510(k), no registration). Do not present SpO2 or blood-pressure outputs as clinical values. Whoop's July 2025 warning letter (Blood Pressure Insights) is the cautionary case (competitors lens).

## India export side
RoDTEP 0.3-4.3% of FOB (rate for 8517.62 not found); exports zero-rated under GST with ITC refund (policy lens, structural).

## Ultrahuman
First UltraFactory: Bengaluru, 2022 (snippet). Indore: not found. The US Plano, TX plant (2024) is modelled on it.

## Certification budget anchor
Predictable Designs: a few thousand dollars to ~USD 50k, wireless implementation is the swing factor. Consistent with the MarkReady module-route figure (USD 3-10k) in the India supplement.
